   499	  "graphlake-sync writes all numbers as decimals. Integers are written without fractional parts."
   500	  [value]

263	(defn- date-value->date-time
264	  "Convert a date value like '2024-01-01+1d-2h' or 'now+3h' into a clj-time DateTime."
265	  [now value]
266	  (when (string? value)
267	    (let [value (query-dsl/patch-minutes-to-months value)
268	          now (if (query-dsl/relative-hourly-value? value)
269	                now
270	                (t/floor now t/day))
271	          [_ date offsets] (re-matches date-value-pattern value)]
272	      (cond
273	        (= "now" date)
274	        (apply-offsets now offsets)
275	
276	        (string? date)
277	        (try (apply-offsets (time-fmt/parse (time-fmt/formatters :date) date) offsets)
278	             (catch Exception _ nil))))))

281	  "A date value resolved against `now`, paired with the precision postgres compares it at: whole
282	   days for everything except an hour-based relative value - see
283	   ardoq.search.query.build/parse-regular-or-relative-date."
284	  [now value]
285	  (when-let [date-time (date-value->date-time now value)]
286	    {:date-time date-time
287	     :precision (if (query-dsl/relative-hourly-value? value) :instant :whole-day)}))

296	  (let [?date (gensym "?date")]

298	          (if (= :instant precision)
299	            [:filter (s/> ?date (->date-time-literal date-time))] ; exclusive of the instant itself
300	            [:filter (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal (day-after date-time)))])))) ; inclusive of the day after

308	  [field from to]
309	  (let [?date (gensym "?date")]
310	    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
311	          [:filter (s/and
312	                    (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal (:date-time from)))
313	                    (if (= :instant (:precision to))
314	                      (s/<= ?date (->date-time-literal (:date-time to)))
315	                      (s/< ?date (->date-time-literal (day-after (:date-time to))))))])))

318	  "`equal` matches the window the value names: the day it falls on, or the hour it falls in for an
319	   hour-based value."

321	  (let [?date (gensym "?date")
322	        [lower span] (if (= :instant precision)
323	                       [(t/floor date-time t/hour) (t/hours 1)]
324	                       [date-time (t/days 1)])]
325	    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
326	          [:filter (s/and (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal lower))

330	  [now {:keys [field operator value] :as advanced-search-rule}]
331	  (let [[from to :as comparands] (map (partial date-value->comparand now)
332	                                      (if (= "between" operator)
333	                                        [(first value) (second value)]
334	                                        [value]))]
335	    (cond
336	      (= "is_empty" operator)
337	      (is-empty->patterns field)
338	
339	      (= "is_not_empty" operator)
340	      (is-not-empty->patterns field)
341	
342	      (some nil? comparands)
343	      (error "Unsupported date value" advanced-search-rule)
344	
345	      (= "equal" operator)
346	      (equal-date->patterns field from)
347	
348	      (= "greater" operator)
349	      (greater-date->patterns field from)
350	
351	      (= "less" operator)
352	      (less-date->patterns field from)
353	
354	      (= "between" operator)
355	      (between-date->patterns field from to)
356

(ns ardoq.graphlake.advanced-search-to-sparql
  (:require
   [ardoq.graphlake.sparql :as s]
   [ardoq.search.query.dsl :as query-dsl]
   [clj-time.core :as t]
   [clj-time.format :as time-fmt]))

(def prefixes
  "Sparql prefixes used throughout the queries.
   The lisp-case keywords are not really valid SparQL, but they work fine in Flint and GraphLake."
  {:rdf "<http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>"
   :rdfs "<http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>"
   :xsd "<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>"
   :sh "<http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#>"
   :ardoq "<http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>"
   :ardoq-common "<http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>"})

(defn error? [result]
  (and (map? result) (:error result)))

(defn error [message rule]
  {:error message
   :rule rule})

(defn ->anchor-patterns
  "A pattern matched by every entity kind we search over (components and references both have
   an id), used to positively bind ?entity for operators that otherwise wouldn't bind it
   themselves (OPTIONAL/NOT EXISTS/UNION-only groups) - without one, such a group evaluates as
   a single graph-wide check disconnected from any specific candidate, instead of per-entity,
   when it ends up alone as an OR branch.
   The query optimizer should fold this into whatever pattern already resolves ?entity from the
   surrounding query, so resolving the id here too should be cheap."
  []
  '[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]])

(defn ->is-component-patterns []
  '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]])

(defn ->reified-reference-triple
  []
  ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)])

(defn ->is-reference-patterns []
  '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]])

(defn ->is-workspace-patterns []
  '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]])

(defn id-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/id binding]])

(defn component-key-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/componentKey binding]])

(defn name-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/name binding]])

(defn description-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/description binding]])

(defn display-text-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/displayText binding]])

(defn created-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/created binding]])

(defn last-updated-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity :ardoq-common/lastUpdated binding]])

(defn created-by-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/createdBy :ardoq-common/id) binding]])

(defn last-modified-by-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/lastModifiedBy :ardoq-common/id) binding]])

(defn root-workspace-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/workspace :ardoq-common/id) binding]])

(defn parent-field->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/parent :ardoq-common/id) binding]])

(defn tags-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/hasTag :ardoq-common/name) binding]])

(defn type-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) binding]])

(defn source-pseudofield->patterns
  "\"source\" is a plain column in postgres, holding the source component's id directly, but a
   reified triple's subject is the component itself rather than a literal id - so here, unlike in
   postgres, it has to be resolved as a pseudofield. Reference search only."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/id binding]])

(defn target-pseudofield->patterns
  "See source-pseudofield->patterns - same reasoning, for the reference's target end."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?targetComponent :ardoq-common/id binding]])

(defn source-component-name-pseudofield->patterns
  "Reference search only."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/name binding]])

(defn target-component-name-pseudofield->patterns
  "Reference search only."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?targetComponent :ardoq-common/name binding]])

(defn source-component-type-pseudofield->patterns
  "Reference search only."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?sourceComponent (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) binding]])

(defn target-component-type-pseudofield->patterns
  "Reference search only."
  [binding]
  [(->reified-reference-triple)
   ['?targetComponent (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) binding]])

(defn parent-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/parent :ardoq-common/name) binding]])

(defn root-workspace-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/workspace :ardoq-common/name) binding]])

(defn created-by-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/createdBy :ardoq-common/name) binding]])

(defn last-modified-by-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :ardoq-common/lastModifiedBy :ardoq-common/name) binding]])

(defn child-count-pseudofield->patterns
  "Unlike the other *->patterns fns, binding must be a variable, not a literal value - the count
   is computed, not looked up, so it can only be projected into a variable."
  [binding]
  [[:where {:select ['?entity [(s/count '?child) binding]]
            ;; We use ->is-component-patterns instead of ->anchor-patterns because only components can have children
            :where (conj (->is-component-patterns)
                         [:optional ['[?child :ardoq-common/parent ?entity]]])
            :group-by ['?entity]}]])

(defn custom-field->patterns [field binding]
  (let [?fieldType (gensym "?fieldType")]
    [[?fieldType :ardoq-common/name field]
     ['?entity ?fieldType binding]]))

(defn field->patterns [field binding]
  (cond
    ;; Built-in fields which can be looked up directly
    (= "_id" field) (id-field->patterns binding)
    (= "component-key" field) (component-key-field->patterns binding)
    (= "name" field) (name-field->patterns binding)
    (= "description" field) (description-field->patterns binding)
    (= "displayText" field) (display-text-field->patterns binding)
    (= "created" field) (created-field->patterns binding)
    (= "last-updated" field) (last-updated-field->patterns binding)

    ;; Built-in fields which require traversing to another entity
    (= "created-by" field) (created-by-field->patterns binding)
    (= "last-modified-by" field) (last-modified-by-field->patterns binding)
    (= "rootWorkspace" field) (root-workspace-field->patterns binding)
    (= "parent" field) (parent-field->patterns binding)
    (= "source" field) (source-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= "target" field) (target-pseudofield->patterns binding)

    ;; Pseudofields which require traversing to another entity
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-tags field) (tags-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-type-name field) (type-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-source-name field) (source-component-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-target-name field) (target-component-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-source-type-name field) (source-component-type-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-target-type-name field) (target-component-type-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-parent-name field) (parent-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-root-workspace-name field) (root-workspace-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-created-by-name field) (created-by-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)
    (= query-dsl/pseudofield-last-modified-by-name field) (last-modified-by-name-pseudofield->patterns binding)

    ;; Pseudofields which require a subquery
    (= "child-count" field) (child-count-pseudofield->patterns binding)

    :else
    (custom-field->patterns field binding)))

(defn equal->patterns [field value]
  (field->patterns field value))

(defn greater->patterns [field value]
  (let [?value (gensym "?value")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?value)
          [:filter (s/> ?value value)])))

(defn less->patterns [field value]
  (let [?value (gensym "?value")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?value)
          [:filter (s/< ?value value)])))

(defn contains-substring->patterns [field value]
  (let [?value (gensym "?value")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?value)
          [:filter (s/contains (s/lcase ?value) (s/lcase value))])))

(defn negate [patterns]
  (conj (->anchor-patterns) [:filter (s/not-exists patterns)]))

(defn not-equal->patterns [field value]
  (negate (equal->patterns field value)))

(defn not-contains-substring->patterns [field value]
  (negate (contains-substring->patterns field value)))

(defn is-empty->patterns [field]
  (let [?value (gensym "?value")]
    (into (->anchor-patterns)
          [[:optional (field->patterns field ?value)]
           [:filter (s/or (s/not (s/bound ?value)) (s/= ?value ""))]])))

(defn is-not-empty->patterns [field]
  (let [?value (gensym "?value")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?value)
          [:filter (s/not= ?value "")])))

(defn child-count-equal->patterns
  "equal->patterns can't be reused as-is for child-count: it plugs value straight in as the
   binding, but child-count->patterns requires binding to be a variable (the count is computed,
   not looked up), so we gensym one and filter on it instead."
  [value]
  (let [?childCount (gensym "?childCount")]
    (conj (child-count-pseudofield->patterns ?childCount)
          [:filter (s/= ?childCount value)])))

(defn child-count-not-equal->patterns
  "Unlike not-equal->patterns (which needs the anchor + NOT EXISTS dance because a field may be
   missing from the graph entirely), child-count-pseudofield->patterns already guarantees
   ?childCount is bound for every component, so a plain not= filter is enough."
  [value]
  (let [?childCount (gensym "?childCount")]
    (conj (child-count-pseudofield->patterns ?childCount)
          [:filter (s/not= ?childCount value)])))

(def ^:private date-value-pattern
  (re-pattern (format "^(\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}|now)((?:%s)*)$" query-dsl/offset-part-pattern)))

(defn- offset->period [[_ sign amount unit]]
  (let [n (cond-> (parse-long amount) (= "-" sign) -)]
    (case unit
      "h" (t/hours n)
      "d" (t/days n)
      "M" (t/months n)
      "y" (t/years n))))

(defn- apply-offsets [date-time offsets]
  (->> (re-seq query-dsl/offset-part-pattern offsets)
       (sort-by (fn [[_ sign]] (if (= "+" sign) 0 1))) ; match postgres in applying all + offsets first
       (map offset->period)
       (reduce t/plus date-time)))

(defn- date-value->date-time
  "Convert a date value like '2024-01-01+1d-2h' or 'now+3h' into a clj-time DateTime."
  [now value]
  (when (string? value)
    (let [value (query-dsl/patch-minutes-to-months value)
          now (if (query-dsl/relative-hourly-value? value)
                now
                (t/floor now t/day))
          [_ date offsets] (re-matches date-value-pattern value)]
      (cond
        (= "now" date)
        (apply-offsets now offsets)

        (string? date)
        (try (apply-offsets (time-fmt/parse (time-fmt/formatters :date) date) offsets)
             (catch Exception _ nil))))))

(defn- date-value->comparand
  "A date value resolved against `now`, paired with the precision postgres compares it at: whole
   days for everything except an hour-based relative value - see
   ardoq.search.query.build/parse-regular-or-relative-date."
  [now value]
  (when-let [date-time (date-value->date-time now value)]
    {:date-time date-time
     :precision (if (query-dsl/relative-hourly-value? value) :instant :whole-day)}))

(defn- ->date-time-literal [date-time]
  (s/cast :xsd/dateTime (time-fmt/unparse (time-fmt/formatters :date-hour-minute-second) date-time)))

(defn- day-after [date-time]
  (t/plus date-time (t/days 1)))

(defn greater-date->patterns [field {:keys [date-time precision] :as comparand}]
  (let [?date (gensym "?date")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
          (if (= :instant precision)
            [:filter (s/> ?date (->date-time-literal date-time))] ; exclusive of the instant itself
            [:filter (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal (day-after date-time)))])))) ; inclusive of the day after

(defn less-date->patterns [field {:keys [date-time] :as comparand}]
  (let [?date (gensym "?date")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
          [:filter (s/< ?date (->date-time-literal date-time))]))) ; exclusive of the bound, day-start or instant alike

(defn between-date->patterns
  [field from to]
  (let [?date (gensym "?date")]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
          [:filter (s/and
                    (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal (:date-time from)))
                    (if (= :instant (:precision to))
                      (s/<= ?date (->date-time-literal (:date-time to)))
                      (s/< ?date (->date-time-literal (day-after (:date-time to))))))])))

(defn equal-date->patterns
  "`equal` matches the window the value names: the day it falls on, or the hour it falls in for an
   hour-based value."
  [field {:keys [date-time precision]}]
  (let [?date (gensym "?date")
        [lower span] (if (= :instant precision)
                       [(t/floor date-time t/hour) (t/hours 1)]
                       [date-time (t/days 1)])]
    (conj (field->patterns field ?date)
          [:filter (s/and (s/>= ?date (->date-time-literal lower))
                          (s/< ?date (->date-time-literal (t/plus lower span))))])))

(defn date-rule->patterns
  [now {:keys [field operator value] :as advanced-search-rule}]
  (let [[from to :as comparands] (map (partial date-value->comparand now)
                                      (if (= "between" operator)
                                        [(first value) (second value)]
                                        [value]))]
    (cond
      (= "is_empty" operator)
      (is-empty->patterns field)

      (= "is_not_empty" operator)
      (is-not-empty->patterns field)

      (some nil? comparands)
      (error "Unsupported date value" advanced-search-rule)

      (= "equal" operator)
      (equal-date->patterns field from)

      (= "greater" operator)
      (greater-date->patterns field from)

      (= "less" operator)
      (less-date->patterns field from)

      (= "between" operator)
      (between-date->patterns field from to)

      :else
      (error "Unsupported date operator" advanced-search-rule))))

(defn has-reference-to-component->patterns [component-id]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType [:ardoq-common/id component-id]]]))

(defn has-reference-to-component-type->patterns [component-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType [(s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) component-type-name]]]))

(defn has-reference-with-type-to-component->patterns [component-id reference-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType [:ardoq-common/id component-id]]]))

(defn has-reference-with-type-to-component-type->patterns [component-type-name reference-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType [(s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) component-type-name]]]))

(defn has-reference-from-component->patterns [component-id]
  (let [?component (gensym "?component")
        ?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     [?component :ardoq-common/id component-id]
     [?component ?referenceType '?entity]]))

(defn has-reference-from-component-type->patterns [component-type-name]
  (let [?component (gensym "?component")
        ?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     [?component (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) component-type-name]
     [?component ?referenceType '?entity]]))

(defn has-reference-with-type-from-component->patterns [component-id reference-type-name]
  (let [?component (gensym "?component")
        ?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     [?component :ardoq-common/id component-id]
     [?component ?referenceType '?entity]]))

(defn has-reference-with-type-from-component-type->patterns [component-type-name reference-type-name]
  (let [?component (gensym "?component")
        ?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     [?component (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) component-type-name]
     [?component ?referenceType '?entity]]))

(defn has-outgoing-reference-type->patterns [reference-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType '_]]))

(defn has-incoming-reference-type->patterns [reference-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['_ ?referenceType '?entity]]))

(defn reference-type-filter-rule->patterns [{:keys [referenceTypeName value] :as advanced-search-rule}]
  (let [reference-operator (query-dsl/clause->reference-operator advanced-search-rule)]
    (cond
      (= "has-reference-to-component" reference-operator)
      (has-reference-with-type-to-component->patterns value referenceTypeName)

      (= "has-reference-to-component-type" reference-operator)
      (has-reference-with-type-to-component-type->patterns value referenceTypeName)

      (= "has-reference-from-component" reference-operator)
      (has-reference-with-type-from-component->patterns value referenceTypeName)

      (= "has-reference-from-component-type" reference-operator)
      (has-reference-with-type-from-component-type->patterns value referenceTypeName)

      (= "has-no-reference-to-component" reference-operator)
      (negate (has-reference-with-type-to-component->patterns value referenceTypeName))

      (= "has-no-reference-to-component-type" reference-operator)
      (negate (has-reference-with-type-to-component-type->patterns value referenceTypeName))

      (= "has-no-reference-from-component" reference-operator)
      (negate (has-reference-with-type-from-component->patterns value referenceTypeName))

      (= "has-no-reference-from-component-type" reference-operator)
      (negate (has-reference-with-type-from-component-type->patterns value referenceTypeName))

      :else
      (error "Unknown reference type operator"
             advanced-search-rule))))

(defn reference-filter-rule->patterns [{:keys [value] :as advanced-search-rule}]
  (let [reference-operator (query-dsl/clause->reference-operator advanced-search-rule)]
    (cond
      (= "has-reference-to-component" reference-operator)

(defn ->decimal-literal
  "graphlake-sync writes all numbers as decimals. Integers are written without fractional parts."
  [value]
  (if (number? value)
    (let [bd (bigdec value)]
      ;; Strip 0 fractional parts, so 1.0 becomes 1, to match graphlake-sync
      (if (zero? (.remainder bd (bigdec 1)))
        (.setScale bd 0)

    value))

(defn and->patterns
  [now {:keys [rules] :as advanced-search-and-rule}]
  (reduce (fn [acc rule]
            (let [result-or-error (advanced-search->sparql-patterns now rule)]
              (if (error? result-or-error)
                (reduced result-or-error)
                (into acc result-or-error))))
          []
          rules))

(defn or->patterns
  [now {:keys [rules] :as advanced-search-or-rule}]
  (reduce (fn [[acc] rule]
            (let [result-or-error (advanced-search->sparql-patterns now rule)]
              (if (error? result-or-error)
                (reduced result-or-error)
                [(conj acc result-or-error)])))
          [[:union]]
          rules))

(defn advanced-search->sparql-patterns
  [now {:keys [condition field operator type value referenceTypeName] :as advanced-search-rule}]
  (let [value (if (= "number" type) (->decimal-literal value) value)]
    (cond
      (= "AND" condition)
      (and->patterns now advanced-search-rule)

      (= "OR" condition)
      (or->patterns now advanced-search-rule)

      ;; Specialized rules for handling certain field, operator and/or type combinations

      (= ["type" "equal" "component"] [field operator value])
      (->is-component-patterns)

      (= ["type" "equal" "reference"] [field operator value])
      (->is-reference-patterns)

      (= ["type" "equal" "workspace"] [field operator value])
      (->is-workspace-patterns)

      (= query-dsl/lucidchart-documents-field field)
      (error "Lucidchart document filtering is not supported in GraphLake advanced search"
             advanced-search-rule)

      (= "date" type)
      (date-rule->patterns now advanced-search-rule)

      (= ["equal" "child-count"] [operator field])
      (child-count-equal->patterns value)

      (= ["not_equal" "child-count"] [operator field])
      (child-count-not-equal->patterns value)

      (and (query-dsl/has-reference--ids field) referenceTypeName)
      (reference-type-filter-rule->patterns advanced-search-rule)

      (query-dsl/reference-filter-clause? advanced-search-rule)
      (reference-filter-rule->patterns advanced-search-rule)

      ;; Standard handling of operators

      (= "equal" operator)
      (equal->patterns field value)

      (= "greater" operator)
      (greater->patterns field value)

      (= "less" operator)
      (less->patterns field value)

      (= "contains_substring" operator)
      (contains-substring->patterns field value)

      (= "not_equal" operator)
      (not-equal->patterns field value)

      (= "not_contains_substring" operator)
      (not-contains-substring->patterns field value)

      (= "is_empty" operator)
      (is-empty->patterns field)

      (= "is_not_empty" operator)
      (is-not-empty->patterns field)

      ;; TODO: support all other operators

      :else
      (error "Unknown operator"
             advanced-search-rule))))

(ns ardoq.graphlake.sparql
  (:refer-clojure :exclude [and >= <= < + > = not= not or count cast cat])
  (:require
   [com.yetanalytics.flint.axiom.impl.format :as flint-format]
   [com.yetanalytics.flint.axiom.protocol :as p]))

;; Fix for flint emitting `1` for `(bigdec 1)`, instead of the expected `"1"^^xsd:decimal`.
;; Filed upstream as yetanalytics/flint#46; remove this once a fixed version ships.
(extend-type java.math.BigDecimal
  p/Literal
  (-valid-literal? [_] true)
  (-format-literal
    ([n] (p/-format-literal n {}))
    ([^java.math.BigDecimal n opts]
     (flint-format/format-literal n (assoc opts :force-iri? (clojure.core/<= (.scale n) 0)))))
  (-format-literal-strval [n] (str n))
  (-format-literal-lang-tag [_] nil)
  (-format-literal-url
    ([n] (p/-format-literal-url n {}))
    ([_ opts] (flint-format/format-xsd-iri "decimal" opts))))

(defn- format-term
  "Format one term of a triple term the way Flint formats the same value in an ordinary triple,
  resolving the shapes Flint resolves: `?var` symbols, `<iri>` strings, `:prefixed/iri` keywords,
  the `a` shorthand for `rdf:type`, and literals. Tried in Flint's own order, so a string is an
  IRI when angle-bracketed and a literal otherwise."
  [term]
  (cond
    (p/-valid-variable? term) (p/-format-variable term)
    (p/-valid-iri? term) (p/-format-iri term)
    (p/-valid-prefix-iri? term) (p/-format-prefix-iri term)
    (p/-valid-rdf-type? term) (p/-format-rdf-type term)
    (p/-valid-literal? term) (p/-format-literal term)
    :else (throw (ex-info "Not a valid SPARQL term" {:term term}))))

;; Stepping-stone: Flint speaks SPARQL 1.1 only (yetanalytics/flint#40), and its triple specs
;; can't be extended from outside the library - the derived specs cache the object spec, so
;; re-defining it in the registry never reaches `format-query`. A triple term therefore rides in
;; through the axiom protocol instead, as a term that formats itself. Drop this for Flint's own
;; syntax once it supports RDF 1.2.
(defrecord TripleTerm [s p o]
  p/IRI
  (-valid-iri? [_] true)
  (-format-iri [_]
    (str "<<( " (format-term s) " " (format-term p) " " (format-term o) " )>>"))
  ;; Flint only unwraps the values of the `:prefixes` map, which a triple term is never one of.
  (-unwrap-iri [this] (p/-format-iri this)))

(defn triple-term
  "4.1 RDF Term Syntax (grammar production [TripleTerm](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#rTripleTerm))

  `<<( subject predicate object )>>`

  An [RDF 1.2 triple term](https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-concepts/#section-triple-terms): a triple
  used as a term in another triple, which is how a reified statement is addressed. graphlake-sync
  writes references this way, so a reference is reached as the `rdf:reifies` subject of the triple
  term holding its source, type and target.

  Valid in object position only. Flint will also accept it as a subject, but SPARQL 1.2 will not.
  The terms inside it are formatted outside Flint's reach, so an inner prefixed IRI is not checked
  against the `:prefixes` map and an inner variable is invisible to Flint's `:bind` and
  expr-as-var scope checks.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(triple-term '?source '?type '?target)` | `<<( ?source ?type ?target )>>` | the reified triple |
  | `['?ref :rdf/reifies (triple-term '?s '?p '?o)]` | `?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?s ?p ?o )>> .` | binds `?ref` to each reifier |
  "
  [subject predicate object]
  (->TripleTerm subject predicate object))

(defmacro cat
  "9.1 Property Path Syntax (SequencePath, `elt1 / elt2`)

  `IRI  (path1 / path2 / ...)`

  Concatenates paths so a triple's predicate matches a sequence of predicates in one step,
  without binding and rejoining through an intermediate variable - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#propertypaths. Used in a triple's predicate position,
  not as a value expression.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(cat :ardoq/Reference :ardoq-common/id)` | `(ardoq:Reference / ardoq-common:id)` | path through Reference then id |
  "
  [& paths]
  (apply list 'list ''cat paths))

(defmacro not
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (unary `!`)

  `xsd:boolean  !(xsd:boolean arg)`

  Logical negation. SPARQL's [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping)
  maps the unary `!` operator to the XPath [fn:not](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#func-not)
  function.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(not true)` | `(!true)` | `false` |
  | `(not (bound ?x))` | `(!BOUND(?x))` | `true` if `?x` is unbound |
  "
  [arg]
  (list 'list ''not arg))

(defmacro <
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (`A < B`)

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 < arg2)`

  Numeric/dateTime less-than. SPARQL's
  [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) maps `<` to
  `op:numeric-less-than` and its dateTime/string equivalents, defined in
  [XPath and XQuery Functions and Operators](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#comp.numeric).

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(< 2 5)` | `(2 < 5)` | `true` |
  | `(< ?date ?today)` | `(?date < ?today)` | `true` if `?date` is before `?today` |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''< arg1 arg2))

(defmacro <=
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (`A <= B`)

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 <= arg2)`

  Numeric/dateTime less-than-or-equal. SPARQL's
  [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) defines `<=` as
  `fn:not(op:numeric-greater-than(arg1, arg2))` - there's no dedicated XPath primitive for it, see
  [XPath and XQuery Functions and Operators](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#comp.numeric).

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(<= 2 5)` | `(2 <= 5)` | `true` |
  | `(<= ?date ?today)` | `(?date <= ?today)` | `true` if `?date` is on or before `?today` |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''<= arg1 arg2))

(defmacro >
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (`A > B`)

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 > arg2)`

  Numeric/dateTime greater-than. SPARQL's
  [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) maps `>` to
  `op:numeric-greater-than` and its dateTime/string equivalents, defined in
  [XPath and XQuery Functions and Operators](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#comp.numeric).

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(> 5 2)` | `(5 > 2)` | `true` |
  | `(> ?childCount 2)` | `(?childCount > 2)` | `true` if `?childCount` is greater than 2 |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''> arg1 arg2))

(defmacro >=
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (`A >= B`)

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 >= arg2)`

  Numeric/dateTime greater-than-or-equal. SPARQL's
  [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) defines `>=` as
  `fn:not(op:numeric-less-than(arg1, arg2))` - there's no dedicated XPath primitive for it, see
  [XPath and XQuery Functions and Operators](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#comp.numeric).

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(>= 5 2)` | `(5 >= 2)` | `true` |
  | `(>= ?date ?today)` | `(?date >= ?today)` | `true` if `?date` is on or after `?today` |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''>= arg1 arg2))

(defmacro +
  "17.3 Operator Mapping (`A + B`)

  `xsd:numeric  (arg1 + arg2)`

  Numeric addition. SPARQL's [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping)
  maps `+` to [op:numeric-add](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#func-numeric-add) - also
  used here to add an `xsd:dayTimeDuration` to an `xsd:dateTime`, per
  [XPath and XQuery Functions and Operators](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#adding-durations-to-dateTimes).

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(+ 2 3)` | `(2 + 3)` | `5` |
  | `(+ ?date (cast :xsd/dayTimeDuration \"PT24H\"))` | `(?date + xsd:dayTimeDuration(\"PT24H\"))` | `?date` plus 24h |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''+ arg1 arg2))

(defmacro bound
  "17.4.1.1 bound

  `xsd:boolean  bound(variable var)`

  Returns `true` if `var` is bound to a value in the current solution, `false` otherwise.
  Unlike most functions, bound takes a variable directly rather than a value expression - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-bound.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(bound ?x)` | `BOUND(?x)` | `true` if `?x` is bound in the current solution |
  | `(bound ?x)` | `BOUND(?x)` | `false` if `?x` is unbound |
  "
  [var]
  (list 'list ''bound var))

(defmacro not-exists
  "17.4.1.4 NOT EXISTS and EXISTS

  `xsd:boolean  NOT EXISTS ( GroupGraphPattern )`

  Tests whether a group graph pattern does not match, given the values already bound by the
  enclosing query. Unlike a value-expression function, NOT EXISTS takes a graph pattern (the same
  vector-of-patterns shape used for `:where`) rather than another expression - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-filter-exists.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(not-exists [[?e :rdf/type ?t]])` | `NOT EXISTS { ?e rdf:type ?t . }` | `true` if `?e` has no `rdf:type` |
  "
  [graph-pattern]
  (list 'list ''not-exists graph-pattern))

(defmacro or
  "17.4.1.5 logical-or

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 || arg2 || ...)`

  The logical-or of the arguments, corresponding to SPARQL's `||` operator - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-logical-or. Per the
  [effective boolean value](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#ebv) rules, an error raised by
  evaluating one argument is suppressed if another argument independently evaluates to `true`.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(or true false)` | `(true \\|\\| false)` | `true` |
  | `(or false false)` | `(false \\|\\| false)` | `false` |
  | `(or (not (bound ?x)) (= ?x \"\"))` | `(!BOUND(?x) \\|\\| (?x = \"\"))` | `true` if `?x` unbound/empty |
  "
  [& args]
  (apply list 'list ''or args))

(defmacro and
  "17.4.1.6 logical-and

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 && arg2 && ...)`

  The logical-and of the arguments, corresponding to SPARQL's `&&` operator - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-logical-and.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(and true true)` | `(true && true)` | `true` |
  | `(and true false)` | `(true && false)` | `false` |
  "
  [& args]
  (apply list 'list ''and args))

(defmacro =
  "17.4.1.7 RDFterm-equal

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 = arg2)`

  Corresponds to [RDFterm-equal](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-RDFterm-equal), which
  SPARQL's [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) maps
  the `=` operator to. Raises an error for incomparable operands rather than returning `false`.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(= ?value \"\")` | `(?value = \"\")` | `true` if `?value` is the empty string |
  | `(= 1 2)` | `(1 = 2)` | `false` |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''= arg1 arg2))

(defmacro not=
  "17.4.1.7 RDFterm-equal (negated)

  `xsd:boolean  (arg1 != arg2)`

  SPARQL's [operator mapping table](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#OperatorMapping) maps
  the `!=` operator to `fn:not(RDFterm-equal(arg1, arg2))` - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-RDFterm-equal.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(not= ?value \"\")` | `(?value != \"\")` | `false` if `?value` is the empty string |
  | `(not= 1 2)` | `(1 != 2)` | `true` |
  "
  [arg1 arg2]
  (list 'list ''not= arg1 arg2))

(defmacro lcase
  "17.4.3.5 LCASE

  `simple literal | xsd:string  LCASE(simple literal | xsd:string ltrl)`

  Converts a string literal to lower case, corresponding to the XPath
  [fn:lower-case](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#func-lower-case) function - see
  https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-lcase.

  | expression | sparql | result |
  |------------|--------|--------|
  | `(lcase \"FooBar\")` | `LCASE(\"FooBar\")` | `\"foobar\"` |
  "
  [ltrl]
  (list 'list ''lcase ltrl))

(defmacro contains

  `xsd:boolean  CONTAINS(string literal arg1, string literal arg2)`

  The CONTAINS function corresponds to the XPath [fn:contains](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#func-contains).
  The arguments must be [argument compatible](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#func-arg-compatibility) otherwise an

(def now
  "A fixed \"current time\" for the date rules: mid-month and mid-day, so both the day
   truncation and the month arithmetic are visible in the expected bounds."
  (time-fmt/parse (time-fmt/formatters :date-time) "2026-03-15T13:45:30.500Z"))

(defn- stabilize-gensyms
  "The generated sparql patterns have bindings with unique automatic names.
   For testing, we translate the __nnnn__auto__ suffixes to a simple incrementing counter,
   so that we can compare the generated patterns to expected patterns."
  [form]
  (let [counter (atom 0)
        suffixes (atom {})]
    (walk/postwalk
     (fn [x]
       (if-let [[full-name base-name] (when (symbol? x)
                                        (re-matches #"\?(.*?)(?:__)?\d+(?:__auto__)?" (name x)))]
         (let [new-suffixes (if (contains? @suffixes full-name)
                              @suffixes
                              (swap! suffixes assoc full-name (swap! counter inc)))
               suffix (get new-suffixes full-name)]
           (symbol (str "?" base-name suffix)))
         x))
     form)))

(deftest advanced-search-rules-are-correctly-translated-to-sparql
  (are [sparql-patterns advanced-search-rule]

             :select '[?entity]
             :where sparql-patterns}
            :pretty? true))

            (->> advanced-search-rule
                 (advanced-search-to-sparql/advanced-search->sparql-patterns now)
                 stabilize-gensyms)))

    '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
      [?entity (cat :ardoq-common/workspace :ardoq-common/id) "e7c901a23f63e6c142f0d4a1"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-string "rootWorkspace" "equal" "e7c901a23f63e6c142f0d4a1"))

    '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
      [?entity (cat :ardoq-common/hasTag :ardoq-common/name) "taggyboi"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-string "_tags" "equal" "taggyboi"))

    '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
      [?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Owns"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-type-name "Owns"))

    ;; References - pseudofields with no component equivalent, resolved via ?sourceComponent/
    ;; ?targetComponent. ->is-reference-patterns does NOT bind these itself - every one of these
    ;; fns brings its own ?entity :rdf/reifies <<(...)>> triple via ->reified-reference-triple, so
    ;; it stays correct standalone even if it ends up alone inside a NOT EXISTS/OPTIONAL/UNION
    ;; branch, where a binding made elsewhere in the query wouldn't be visible anyway.

    ;; "source"/"target" are plain id columns in postgres, but a reified triple's subject/object
    ;; are the components themselves, so their id has to be looked up rather than compared directly.
    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/id "f789a3ce676823586995e7ce"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-string "source" "equal" "f789a3ce676823586995e7ce"))

    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?targetComponent :ardoq-common/id "1618efd4e8aa7668bda715bb"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-string "target" "equal" "1618efd4e8aa7668bda715bb"))

    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/name "Ardoq"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-source-component-name "equal" "Ardoq"))

    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?targetComponent :ardoq-common/name "GraphLake"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-target-component-name "equal" "GraphLake"))

    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?sourceComponent (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Application"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-source-component-type "equal" "Application"))

    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?targetComponent (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Application"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference (dqu/by-target-component-type "equal" "Application"))

    ;; Both ends filtered in the same query - each clause brings its own copy of the fixed-name
    ;; reifies triple, and that's fine: they describe the same fact about the same ?entity, so the
    ;; duplicate join is a no-op rather than a conflict.
    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/name "Ardoq"]
     ['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
     ['?targetComponent :ardoq-common/name "GraphLake"]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference
                   (dqu/by-source-component-name "equal" "Ardoq")
                   (dqu/by-target-component-name "equal" "GraphLake"))

    ;; Regression test for the reason each fn self-anchors: since ->is-reference-patterns binds
    ;; nothing here, ?sourceComponent would otherwise be unbound inside the NOT EXISTS, turning
    ;; "source != X" into a graph-wide "does any component have id X" check instead of a
    ;; per-reference one.
    [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     [:union
      [['?entity :ardoq-common/id '_]
       [:filter (s/not-exists
                 [['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
                  ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/id "f789a3ce676823586995e7ce"]])]]
      [['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]
       ['?sourceComponent :ardoq-common/id "1618efd4e8aa7668bda715bb"]]]]
    (dqu/query-for :reference
                   (dqu/or (dqu/by-string "source" "not_equal" "f789a3ce676823586995e7ce")
                           (dqu/by-string "source" "equal" "1618efd4e8aa7668bda715bb")))

    ;; Workspaces

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/id "1195fcaa491fe77392a3cc93"]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-string "_id" "equal" "1195fcaa491fe77392a3cc93"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/name "Applications"]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-string "name" "equal" "Applications"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/description "All our applications"]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-string "description" "equal" "All our applications"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/created ?date1]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T00:00:00"))
                    (< ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-16T00:00:00")))]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-date "created" "equal" "now+0d"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity (cat :ardoq-common/createdBy :ardoq-common/id) "6a93de0f631cc5d3fa042d69"]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-string "created-by" "equal" "6a93de0f631cc5d3fa042d69"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/lastUpdated ?date1]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-02-02T00:00:00"))
                    (< ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-02-03T00:00:00")))]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-date "last-updated" "equal" "2026-02-02"))

    '[[?entity :rdf/type :ardoq/Workspace]
      [?entity (cat :ardoq-common/lastModifiedBy :ardoq-common/id) "6a93de0f631cc5d3fa042d69"]]
    (dqu/query-for :workspace (dqu/by-string "last-modified-by" "equal" "6a93de0f631cc5d3fa042d69"))

    ;; Compound rules

    '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]
      [?entity :ardoq-common/name "GraphLake"]]
    (dqu/query-for :component
                   (dqu/by-string "name" "equal" "GraphLake"))

    '[[:union
       [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]]
       [[?entity :ardoq-common/name "GraphLake"]]]]
    (dqu/or (#'dqu/type-rule :component)
            (dqu/by-string "name" "equal" "GraphLake"))

    ;; Different operators

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/name ?value1]
      [:filter (contains (lcase ?value1) (lcase "Lake"))]]
    (dqu/by-string "name" "contains_substring" "Lake")

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]
      [:filter (not-exists [[?entity :ardoq-common/name ?value1]
                            [:filter (contains (lcase ?value1) (lcase "Lake"))]])]]
    (dqu/by-string "name" "not_contains_substring" "Lake")

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]
      [:filter (not-exists [[?entity :ardoq-common/id "1195fcaa491fe77392a3cc93"]])]]
    (dqu/by-string "_id" "not_equal" "1195fcaa491fe77392a3cc93")

    '[[:where {:select [?entity [(count ?child) ?childCount1]]
               :where [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]
                       [:optional [[?child :ardoq-common/parent ?entity]]]]
               :group-by [?entity]}]
      [:filter (not= ?childCount1 2M)]]
    (dqu/by-number "child-count" "not_equal" 2)

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]
      [:optional [[?entity :ardoq-common/description ?value1]]]
      [:filter (or (not (bound ?value1)) (= ?value1 ""))]]
    (dqu/is-empty "description" "string")

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/description ?value1]
      [:filter (not= ?value1 "")]]
    (dqu/is-not-empty "description" "string")

    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "priority"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?value2]
      [:filter (> ?value2 5M)]]
    (dqu/by-number "priority" "greater" 5)

    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "priority"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?value2]
      [:filter (< ?value2 5M)]]
    (dqu/by-number "priority" "less" 5)

    ;; Date operators. Postgres compares whole days, so every bound is the start of a day and
    ;; the range is half-open - see ardoq.search.query.build/round-range-map.

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/created ?date1]
      [:filter (>= ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-07T00:00:00"))]]
    (dqu/by-date "created" "greater" "now-9d")

    ;; "m" is minutes to the frontend but months to us, and is patched before parsing.
    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/created ?date1]
      [:filter (>= ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-01-16T00:00:00"))]]
    (dqu/by-date "created" "greater" "now-2m")

    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/lastUpdated ?date1]
      [:filter (< ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-02-02T00:00:00"))]]
    (dqu/by-date "last-updated" "less" "2026-02-02")

    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "review_date"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?date2]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-01-01T00:00:00"))
                    (< ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-02-16T00:00:00")))]]
    (dqu/by-date "review_date" "between" ["2026-01-01" "now-1M"])

    ;; An hour-based relative value is compared at instant precision, untruncated.
    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/created ?date1]
      [:filter (> ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T15:45:30"))]]
    (dqu/by-date "created" "greater" "now+2h")

    ;; Each end of a between is resolved on its own, so an hour-based lower bound leaves the
    ;; absolute upper one comparing whole days.
    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "review_date"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?date2]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T11:45:30"))
                    (< ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-04-02T00:00:00")))]]
    (dqu/by-date "review_date" "between" ["now-2h" "2026-04-01"])

    ;; An hour-based upper bound is inclusive, unlike the whole-day case above.
    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "review_date"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?date2]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-01-01T00:00:00"))
                    (<= ?date2 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T15:45:30")))]]
    (dqu/by-date "review_date" "between" ["2026-01-01" "now+2h"])

    ;; An hour-based equal matches the hour the value falls in, following ardoq.search.predicate
    ;; rather than postgres, whose range for this is empty unless the query runs after 23:00.
    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/created ?date1]
      [:filter (and (>= ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T15:00:00"))
                    (< ?date1 (:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T16:00:00")))]]
    (dqu/by-date "created" "equal" "now+2h")

    ;; is_empty/is_not_empty don't resolve a value against `now` - a date field is empty or it
    ;; isn't regardless of type - so they use the same type-agnostic patterns as any other field.
    '[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]
      [:optional [[?entity :ardoq-common/created ?value1]]]
      [:filter (or (not (bound ?value1)) (= ?value1 ""))]]
    (dqu/is-empty "created" "date")

    '[[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "review_date"]
      [?entity ?fieldType1 ?value2]
      [:filter (not= ?value2 "")]]
    (dqu/is-not-empty "review_date" "date")

    {:error "Unsupported date value"
     :rule (dqu/by-date "created" "greater" "last tuesday")}
    (dqu/by-date "created" "greater" "last tuesday")

    {:error "Unsupported date value"
     :rule (dqu/by-date "created" "between" "last tuesday")}
    (dqu/by-date "created" "between" "last tuesday")

    {:error "Unsupported date value"
     :rule (dqu/by-date "created" "between" ["last tuesday"])}
    (dqu/by-date "created" "between" ["last tuesday"])

    {:error "Unknown operator"
     :rule (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")}
    (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")

    ;; Error handling

    {:error "Unknown operator"
     :rule (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")}
    (dqu/and (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")
             (#'dqu/type-rule :component))

    {:error "Unknown operator"
     :rule (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")}
    (dqu/or (dqu/by-string "name" "foobar" "Lake")
            (#'dqu/type-rule :component))

    ;; Gensyms
    '[[:union
       [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Control"]]
       [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Risk"]]]]
    (dqu/or (dqu/by-type-name "Control")
            (dqu/by-type-name "Risk"))

    ;; Complete examples
    '[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]
      [:union
       [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Control"]]
       [[?entity :ardoq-common/name ?value1]
        [:filter (contains (lcase ?value1) (lcase "ackup"))]]]]
    (dqu/query-for :component
                   (dqu/or (dqu/by-type-name "Control")
                           (dqu/by-string "name" "contains_substring" "ackup")))))

(ns ardoq.graphlake.sparql-test
  (:require
   [ardoq.graphlake.sparql :as s]
   [clojure.test :refer [deftest is are testing]]
   [com.yetanalytics.flint :as flint]))

(def ^:private prefixes
  {:rdf "<http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>"
   :ardoq-common "<http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>"
   :xsd "<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>"})

(defn- where->sparql
  "Format `where` as a query and return just the body of the WHERE clause."
  [where]
  (->> (flint/format-query {:prefixes prefixes :select '[?ref] :where where})
       (re-find #"WHERE \{ (.*) \}$")
       second))

(deftest triple-term-formats-as-a-sparql-1-2-triple-term
  (are [expected term]
       (= expected (where->sparql [['?ref :rdf/reifies term]]))

    "?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?source ?type ?target )>> ."
    (s/triple-term '?source '?type '?target)

    "?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?source ardoq-common:name ?target )>> ."
    (s/triple-term '?source :ardoq-common/name '?target)

    "?ref rdf:reifies <<( <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/abc> a ?target )>> ."
    (s/triple-term "<http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/abc>" 'a '?target)

    "?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?source ardoq-common:name \"Owns\" )>> ."
    (s/triple-term '?source :ardoq-common/name "Owns")))

(deftest triple-term-composes-with-the-rest-of-the-where-clause
  (is (= "?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?source ?type ?target )>> . ?ref ardoq-common:name ?name ."
         (where->sparql [['?ref :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?source '?type '?target)]
                         ['?ref :ardoq-common/name '?name]]))))

(deftest triple-term-rejects-a-term-that-is-not-a-sparql-term
  (testing "a bare symbol is neither a variable nor the rdf:type shorthand"

    (is (= "?entity ardoq-common:name 11875.5 ."

1. DATE/NUMBER HANDLING

Dates: typed `xsd:dateTime` literals, always. `advanced_search_to_sparql.clj:289-290`:
```clojure
(defn- ->date-time-literal [date-time]
  (s/cast :xsd/dateTime (time-fmt/unparse (time-fmt/formatters :date-hour-minute-second) date-time)))
```
Produces e.g. `(:xsd/dateTime "2026-03-15T00:00:00")` → SPARQL `xsd:dateTime("2026-03-15T00:00:00")` (test evidence: `advanced_search_to_sparql_test.clj:188-190`). Value comes from clj-time (`clj-time.core`/`clj-time.format`), resolved against `now` with day/hour truncation logic (`date-value->date-time` L263-278, `date-value->comparand` L280-287).

Numbers: `BigDecimal` values, via `->decimal-literal` (L498-507):
```clojure
(defn ->decimal-literal [value]
  (if (number? value)
    (let [bd (bigdec value)]
      (if (zero? (.remainder bd (bigdec 1)))
        (.setScale bd 0)
        bd))
    value))
```
Applied in `advanced-search->sparql-patterns` L533: `(if (= "number" type) (->decimal-literal value) value)`. Test: `child-count "equal" 2` → `(= ?childCount1 2M)` (L235), `priority "greater" 5` → `(> ?value2 5M)` (L439).

**BigDecimal shim (sparql.clj:7-20)**: Flint's default literal formatting for `(bigdec 1)` emits bare `1`, not `"1"^^xsd:decimal` — a bug (filed upstream yetanalytics/flint#46). The shim `extend-type java.math.BigDecimal p/Literal` forces integral-scale decimals (`scale <= 0`, i.e. no fractional part) to format as an explicit typed literal `"11875"^^xsd:decimal`, while decimals with a fractional part format as a bare literal `11875.5` (relies on Flint's native decimal literal support, which alone is unambiguous). Confirmed by `sparql_test.clj:48-55`:
```clojure
"?entity ardoq-common:name \"11875\"^^xsd:decimal ."   ; 11875M
"?entity ardoq-common:name 11875.5 ."                    ; 11875.5M
```
Implication: numeric literals ARE typed (`xsd:decimal`) when they'd otherwise be ambiguous with an integer/IRI-like bare number; GraphLake's underlying store (graphlake-sync) always writes numbers as decimals with integers stripped of trailing `.0`, so the shim exists purely to match that on-the-wire representation exactly, not to add typing generally.

2. REIFICATION

`->reified-reference-triple` (L39-41) — `['?entity :rdf/reifies (s/triple-term '?sourceComponent '?referenceType '?targetComponent)]` — is used ONLY by the 6 pseudofield fns needing properties OF the reference triple's endpoints: `source-pseudofield->patterns` (L88-94), `target-pseudofield->patterns` (L96-100), `source-component-name-pseudofield->patterns` (L102-106), `target-component-name-pseudofield->patterns` (L108-112), `source-component-type-pseudofield->patterns` (L114-118), `target-component-type-pseudofield->patterns` (L120-124). Doc comment on `source-pseudofield->patterns` (L88-91): "source" is a plain postgres column holding the id directly, but a reified triple's subject is the component itself, so it must be resolved as a pseudofield **for reference search only**.

Ordinary component-to-component traversal (has-reference-to/from-component, outgoing/incoming reference type, etc., L360-422) uses PLAIN triples `['?entity ?referenceType target]` / `[?component ?referenceType '?entity]` — never reification. Reification is needed only when the query needs to bind the reference's source/target/type as *terms* to query properties of them; a reference used purely as an edge (traverse through it) needs no reification since the reference type IRI itself is the predicate.

3. SPARQL VERSION

Confirmed RDF 1.2 triple-term syntax IS emitted. `sparql.clj:36-40` comment: "Flint speaks SPARQL 1.1 only (yetanalytics/flint#40)... A triple term therefore rides in through the axiom protocol instead... Drop this for Flint's own syntax once it supports RDF 1.2." The `TripleTerm` record formats as `<<( s p o )>>` (L41-47), confirmed literal output in `sparql_test.clj:23`: `"?ref rdf:reifies <<( ?source ?type ?target )>> ."` — this is RDF 1.2 triple-term grammar (`<<( )>>`), not RDF-star's `<< >>`. `triple-term` docstring (L49-70) cites the actual SPARQL 1.2 spec (`sparql12-query/#rTripleTerm`) and RDF 1.2 concepts spec. Whether GraphLake's backend accepts this: not found in this repo — no explicit confirmation/rejection in gateway/service/api files; the assumption is implicit (graphlake-sync writes references this way per L88-91 comment, and it's exercised by passing tests), but nothing in this repo asserts GraphLake's SPARQL engine version/compatibility explicitly.

4. FIXED VOCABULARY INVENTORY

Prefixes (L8-16):
- `rdf`: `http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#`
- `rdfs`: `http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#`
- `xsd`: `http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#`
- `sh`: `http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#`
- `ardoq`: `http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/`
- `ardoq-common`: `http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/`

Terms used throughout, with meaning:
- `:rdf/type` — entity's type IRI (component type / reference type / "a")
- `:rdf/reifies` — links a reification entity to the `TripleTerm` it reifies (a reference's own IRI reifies its source/type/target triple)
- `:rdfs/subClassOf` — type hierarchy edge; `(cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf)` walks two levels to reach `:ardoq/Component` or `:ardoq/Reference` (the fixed root classes)
- `:rdfs/label` — human-readable type name (component type name / reference type name)
- `:ardoq/Component` — root class for all component types
- `:ardoq/Reference` — root class for all reference types
- `:ardoq/Workspace` — workspace type (single level, no subClassOf walk)
- `:ardoq/CustomFieldType` — class of custom field-type nodes (`custom-field-patterns`, L603-608)
- `:sh/targetClass`, `:sh/property`, `:sh/path` — SHACL vocabulary used to find which custom field types target a given entity's class (`(inv :sh/targetClass)` — inverse path — L606)
- `:ardoq-common/id` — entity id (also the anchor pattern field, L34)
- `:ardoq-common/componentKey` — component key
- `:ardoq-common/name` — component/workspace name; also custom field name lookup value
- `:ardoq-common/description` — description field
- `:ardoq-common/displayText` — reference's display text (reference's name-equivalent)
- `:ardoq-common/created`, `:ardoq-common/lastUpdated` — timestamps
- `:ardoq-common/createdBy`, `:ardoq-common/lastModifiedBy` — user references, traversed then `:ardoq-common/id` or `:ardoq-common/name`
- `:ardoq-common/workspace` — root workspace reference, traversed then `:id`/`:name`
- `:ardoq-common/parent` — parent component reference, traversed then `:id`/`:name`
- `:ardoq-common/hasTag` — tag reference, traversed then `:ardoq-common/name`
- `:ardoq-common/color`, `:ardoq-common/icon`, `:ardoq-common/image` — component styling fields (only in `component-field-patterns`, L610-654, not in `field->patterns`)
- `:ardoq-common/componentTypeId`, `:ardoq-common/modelId` — traversed via `(cat :rdf/type ...)` for `typeId`/`model` frontend fields (component-field-patterns only)

5. CANONICAL PATTERNS (exact quotes)

Find component by type name (test `advanced_search_to_sparql_test.clj:544-551`, full compound example):
```clojure
'[[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Component]
  [:union
   [[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Control"]]
   [[?entity :ardoq-common/name ?value1]
    [:filter (contains (lcase ?value1) (lcase "ackup"))]]]]
```
Simpler standalone "by type name" (L176 test, `type-name-pseudofield->patterns`, source L85-86):
```clojure
(defn type-name-pseudofield->patterns [binding]
  [['?entity (s/cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) binding]])
```
→ `[?entity (cat :rdf/type :rdfs/label) "Application"]`

Read a custom field value (`custom-field->patterns`, L148-151):
```clojure
(defn custom-field->patterns [field binding]
  (let [?fieldType (gensym "?fieldType")]
    [[?fieldType :ardoq-common/name field]
     ['?entity ?fieldType binding]]))
```
Test-verified: `[?fieldType1 :ardoq-common/name "support_level"] [?entity ?fieldType1 "Premium"]` (L238-240).

Traverse an outgoing reference of a named type (`has-outgoing-reference-type->patterns`, L412-416):
```clojure
(defn has-outgoing-reference-type->patterns [reference-type-name]
  (let [?referenceType (gensym "?referenceType")]
    [[?referenceType :rdfs/label reference-type-name]
     [?referenceType (s/cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
     ['?entity ?referenceType '_]]))
```
Test-quoted exact form (L149-152):
```clojure
'[[?referenceType1 :rdfs/label "Owns"]
  [?referenceType1 (cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
  [?entity ?referenceType1 _]]
```

Traverse an incoming reference of a named type (`has-incoming-reference-type->patterns`, L418-422), test-quoted (L160-163):
```clojure
'[[?referenceType1 :rdfs/label "Owns"]
  [?referenceType1 (cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
  [_ ?referenceType1 ?entity]]
```
(Same pattern, subject/object swapped — `[_ ?referenceType ?entity]` vs `[?entity ?referenceType '_]`.)

Negation / does-not-have (`negate`, L208-209):
```clojure
(defn negate [patterns]
  (conj (->anchor-patterns) [:filter (s/not-exists patterns)]))
```
Test-quoted exact form for "does-not-have-outgoing-reference-type" (L154-158):
```clojure
'[[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]
  [:filter (not-exists [[?referenceType1 :rdfs/label "Owns"]
                        [?referenceType1 (cat :rdfs/subClassOf :rdfs/subClassOf) :ardoq/Reference]
                        [?entity ?referenceType1 _]])]]
```
The `[?entity :ardoq-common/id _]` anchor pattern is required so `?entity` is positively bound before the NOT EXISTS filter (see `->anchor-patterns` docstring, L25-32) — otherwise a lone negated branch (e.g. inside an OR) has no per-entity binding to filter against.
